- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- Model often overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 0.5–1.5% per day for 3–7 days post-spike.  
- Forecast mean reversion is weak in early horizon (1–7 days); if forecast is 5%+ above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day for 3–5 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model frequently misses downward trends in sentiment-heavy periods; if sentiment is negative for 3+ consecutive days, add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead of true trend direction.
